newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli minister opposes agriculture reforms.
newsitem.headline: Israeli minister opposes agriculture reforms.

text.p: Israel's Agriculture Minister Rafael Eitan has said he is vehemently opposed to a Treasury proposal to lift all restrictions on fruit and vegetable imports, the Agriculture Ministry said on Wednesday.
A statement by the ministry said that Eitan phoned Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman on Wednesday to "vehemently complain" against the Treasury proposal.
"This will not be nor will there be anything like it," Eitan was said to have told Neeman.
The proposal is one of more than a hundred economic reforms that will be brought to cabinet on Sunday, the Agriculture Ministry said.

The Treasury spokesman refused to confirm the existence of the proposal saying the Treasury will comment on these matters only when ministers have had the opportunity to see the proposals contained in a 300-page document.
The current restrictions on fruit and vegetable imports, including duties, have been in place for many years in order to protect Israeli farmers and to ensure a readily available domestic market.

Agriculture ministry director general Danny Krichman said the plan, if implemented, will lead to many farmers abandoning the agriculture sector. He described the proposed policy as "contrary to the actions of other states".

The proposal would be the latest in a series of measures aimed at exposing the domestic economy to foreign competition which the Treasury hopes will lead to lower prices and better quality consumer products.

The more than a hundred proposals in the 300-page document, due to be brought to the cabinet for discussion on Sunday, have been requested by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in an effort to restore economic growth in 1998.
